title: Make an alteration finite over a modification
statement: Let $a:T\to S$ be an alteration of reduced Noetherian schemes [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. There exist modifications $u:\widetilde T\to T$ and $v:S'\to S$ and a finite surjective morphism $p:\widetilde T\to S'$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] such that $a u=v p$. If $S$ is integral, the schemes $S'$ and $\widetilde T$ may be taken reduced, with $S'$ integral when $T$ is integral.

source.place: Lemma 2.5, p. 4 (flattening of an alteration). Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Suppose first that $S$ is integral. The alteration definition [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data] gives properness, surjectivity and a dense open over which $a$ is finite. Properness gives finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation] on the integral base and intersect its nonempty open with the finite locus; take a nonempty affine open $U$ in that intersection. Then $a_U$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, hence finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The Noetherian base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (every open and every intersection of affine opens is quasi-compact), so [lem-trf-finite-after-blowup] applies. Obtain a $U$-admissible blow-up $v:S'\to S$ and a finite locally free strict transform $p:\widetilde T\to S'$. Let $u:\widetilde T\to T$ be the other projection. The fibre-product identity is $a u=v p$.

Write $\mathcal I$ for the admissible ideal and $W=S\setminus V(\mathcal I)$; then $U\subseteq W$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. On an affine integral open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, the blow-up is covered by $\operatorname{Spec}A[I/f]$ for generators $f$ of $I$, by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] and the local gluing construction [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data]. A chart with $f=0$ is empty. For $f\ne0$, its ring is the subalgebra $A[I/f]\subseteq A_f$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], hence a domain; the chart contains the lift of the generic point of $S$. Thus all nonempty charts have that common generic point, so $S'$ is irreducible and reduced, and is nonempty since it contains $U$. This proves that $S'$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], without assuming that $T$ is integral. The identification over $W$ supplied by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement] (apply it also with $Y=X=S$) identifies $v^{-1}(U)$ with $U$. It is now a nonempty open of an integral scheme, so it is dense. Properness of $v$ follows from [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper]; hence $v$ is a modification.

source.place: Lemma 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), affine-chart proof; the centre misses U

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement], the open of $\widetilde T$ lying over $W$ is $T_W$ and $u$ is the identity under this identification. By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], $\widetilde T$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of this open inside $T\times_S S'$. Thus it is closed there. The projection $T\times_S S'\to T$ is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] applied to $v$; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes $u$ proper. The closure theorem [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] applies to the open immersion $T_W\hookrightarrow T\times_S S'$: the ambient scheme is Noetherian (the blow-up is of finite type and $T$ is Noetherian), so the immersion is quasi-compact and the ambient is quasi-separated. It gives an injection $\mathcal O_{\widetilde T}\hookrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_{T_W}$. Every nonempty open of $\widetilde T$ therefore meets $T_W$: otherwise its section ring injects into zero and that open is empty. Moreover $T_W$ is reduced since $T$ is reduced, so the same injection kills every nilpotent section. Consequently $\widetilde T$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Strict-transform closure, with the quasi-compact open-immersion closure theorem

proof.text: Every irreducible component of $T$ dominates $S$ by [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Therefore its generic point maps to the generic point of $S$ and lies in $T_U$; hence $T_U$ is dense in $T$, and also dense in $T_W$. Since $T_W$ is dense in $\widetilde T$ and $T_U$ identifies with its restriction over $U$, the inverse image $u^{-1}(T_U)$ is dense in $\widetilde T$. Together with properness and the isomorphism over $T_U$, this proves that $u$ is a modification. The map $p$ is finite [def-pc-finite-locally-free], hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its image contains $v^{-1}(U)$ because there it is the surjective map $T_U\to U$. That open is dense in $S'$, so the closed image is all of $S'$. This proves the integral-base case, including both reducedness conclusions. Record also the following feature of this construction: for any nonempty open $V\subseteq U$, the same domination argument makes $T_V$ dense in $T_W$, hence its lift is dense in $\widetilde T$; and $v^{-1}(V)$ is dense in the integral $S'$. This permits later shrinking of $U$.

source.place: Integral-base construction: domination, density, and closed-image surjectivity (01W1, 01WG)

proof.text: Now let $S$ be any nonempty reduced Noetherian scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], enumerate its components $S_1,\ldots,S_n$, and the components $C_1,\ldots,C_m$ of $T$. Give each component its reduced closed subscheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; each $S_i$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The alteration domination clause assigns each $C_j$ to the unique component $S_{i(j)}$ it dominates. Properness implies that $a(C_j)$ is closed, hence it equals $S_{i(j)}$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Surjectivity and finiteness of the component covers imply that every $S_i$ occurs: if it did not, its generic point would lie in another component. Let $T_i$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\bigcup_{i(j)=i}C_j\subseteq T$. This is a finite closed union. The same reduced-source factorization lemma [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives a morphism $a_i:T_i\to S_i$ satisfying $a j_i=\iota_i a_i$, where $j_i:T_i\hookrightarrow T$ and $\iota_i:S_i\hookrightarrow S$.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ component reduction, with 01J3/01J4 (reduced structures) and 0356 (factorization)

proof.text: Each $a_i$ is an alteration of reduced Noetherian schemes with integral base. To check properness, the factor map $T_i\to T\times_S S_i$ is a closed immersion: it is the base change of $j_i$ along $T\times_S S_i\to T$, since $T_i\times_S S_i\cong T_i$ (a morphism factoring through a closed immersion has this pullback). Use [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change], then [lem-pc-proper-base-change] for $a$, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] for the composite. Surjectivity follows from $a(C_j)=S_i$ for every component in this nonempty group. Its components are exactly these $C_j$, and all dominate $S_i$. If $F\subseteq S$ is the original dense finite locus, then $F\cap S_i$ contains the generic point of $S_i$. Over it the displayed closed immersion embeds $T_i|_F$ into the base change of the finite $T_F\to F$. This restricted map is finite: on an affine open its algebra is a quotient of a finite module algebra, hence finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Thus every hypothesis used in the integral construction is satisfied by $a_i$.

source.place: Componentwise properness and generic finiteness; Tags 01W4, 01W5, 035C, 0356

proof.text: The intermediate component-separation square has vertical arrows $\coprod_i a_i:\coprod_iT_i\to\coprod_iS_i$ and $a:T\to S$, and horizontal arrows $q=\coprod_i j_i$ and $r=\coprod_i\iota_i$; it commutes because $a j_i=\iota_i a_i$. These coproducts exist by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Both $q$ and $r$ are finite: on an affine open their inverse images have rings $\prod_i A/I_i$, finite modules over $A$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put $W=S\setminus\bigcup_{i\ne k}(S_i\cap S_k)$. This dense open is the disjoint union of the component opens $W_i$. Over $W$, $r$ is an isomorphism, and over $T_W$ so is $q$: $T_i|_{W_i}$ is the full reduced open $T|_{W_i}$, while every other summand is empty. The equality of reduced structures follows from uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Domination ensures that $T_W$ is dense in $T$, and $T_i|_{W_i}$ is dense in $T_i$. Likewise $W_i$ is dense in $S_i$. Since finite maps are proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], $q$ and $r$ are modifications. In particular the reduction is on the full $S_i$ and $T_i$, not on the open strata $W_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ: separation of components over the complement of their pairwise intersections

proof.text: Apply the integral-base construction of steps 1--4 to each full morphism $a_i:T_i\to S_i$. Obtain $u_i:\widetilde T_i\to T_i$, $v_i:S'_i\to S_i$, and finite surjective $p_i:\widetilde T_i\to S'_i$ with $a_i u_i=v_i p_i$. Keep the nonempty open $U_i\subseteq S_i$ chosen there: $v_i$ is an isomorphism over $U_i$, $u_i$ over $a_i^{-1}(U_i)$, and both lifted opens remain dense after any nonempty open shrink of $U_i$ by step 4. Set $S'=\coprod_i S'_i$, $\widetilde T=\coprod_i\widetilde T_i$, $p=\coprod_i p_i$, $v|_{S'_i}=\iota_i v_i$, and $u|_{\widetilde T_i}=j_i u_i$. These maps exist uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. On each summand, $a u=a j_i u_i=\iota_i a_i u_i=\iota_i v_i p_i=v p$. The map $p$ is finite and surjective: this is checked on the open-and-closed target summands $S'_i$, where it is exactly $p_i$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Finite component assembly of the integral construction (Tag 0BAJ reduction)

proof.text: The maps $\coprod_i u_i$ and $\coprod_i v_i$ are proper. Indeed their restrictions to the open-and-closed target summands are the given proper maps: after any base change the image of a closed set is closed on each summand, finite type is checked by the affine-open definition, and the diagonal has the given closed diagonals as its diagonal blocks and empty off-diagonal blocks [def-weil-proper-morphism]. This directly checks all three defining conditions. Since $u=q(\coprod_i u_i)$ and $v=r(\coprod_i v_i)$, the proper-composition theorem [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] gives properness of $u$ and $v$.

source.place: Properness of the assembled arrows; Tag 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-component-coproduct] to the full component inclusions $S_i\hookrightarrow S$ and the dense opens $U_i$. It supplies a dense open $V\subseteq S$ over which $r$ is an isomorphism and whose restriction to each $S_i$ is contained in $U_i$. Replace $V$ by $V\cap W$, with $W$ as in step 7. It still contains every component generic point. Over $V$, the maps $v_i$ identify $S'|_V$ with $\coprod_i(S_i\cap V)=V$. The maps $u_i$ identify $\widetilde T|_V$ with $\coprod_i T_i|_V=T|_V$. Thus $v$ and $u$ are isomorphisms over $V$ and $T_V$, respectively. Domination makes $T_V$ dense in $T$. Each nonempty $V\cap S_i$ is an open shrink of $U_i$; the density property from step 4 makes its inverse image dense in both $S'_i$ and $\widetilde T_i$. Therefore the inverse images of $V$ and $T_V$ are dense in $S'$ and $\widetilde T$. Along with step 9 this proves that $u,v$ are modifications [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. If $S=\varnothing$, then $T=\varnothing$; take the two empty schemes and identity maps. This handles the empty case as well and completes the unchanged statement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_surjective_refinement {T S : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced T] [IsReduced S] [IsNoetherian T] [IsNoetherian S] (a : T ⟶ S) (ha : IsAlteration a) : ∃ (T' S' : Scheme.{u}) (u : T' ⟶ T) (v : S' ⟶ S) (p : T' ⟶ S'), IsModification u ∧ IsModification v ∧ IsFinite p ∧ Surjective p ∧ u ≫ a = p ≫ v ∧ (IsIntegral S → IsReduced S' ∧ IsReduced T' ∧ (IsIntegral T → IsIntegral S'))
